terra.problem: The passage does not say Amos spent his whole life around grass.
The verse does not say the gates come down before the rulers are cut off. It also mentions a scepter only for the one in Beth-eden, not both rulers.
“I won't dress it up” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
Calling Tyre a rich trading city introduces a fact outside the passage without a reference.
“We all wish” assumes how the baker feels.
The text calls it a covenant of brotherhood; it does not say the covenant was between brothers.
The oven-timer joke makes light of Edom's continual anger in a charge involving violence and lack of compassion.
“I won't joke about it” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
“I'll just say it straight” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
The explanation assumes the baker wanted a softer ending.
“I'll leave it as the LORD says it” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
“I'll say it plainly and move on” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
The passage identifies Amos as a sheepherder, not a prophet. Calling him a prophet requires a reference outside the passage.
The verse says Judah's fathers walked in the lies, not that the lies began before the fathers. It also does not establish what role the current king had.
